finding.claim: SQL injection via unvalidated $_GET['sort'] concatenated into ORDER BY in list_users_sorted; no allowlist, no escaping. Conditional: no call site exists in the repo.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: concatenated into ORDER BY and executed via query()

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, no escaping/quoting (ORDER BY cannot use bind placeholders), return value not checked, no auth/ownership check in file. Caveat: list_users_sorted is never called in the repo, so direct requests to list.php do not reach it; any caller that passes the request param exposes the injection. SQLite accepts CASE and scalar subqueries in ORDER BY, enabling boolean-based blind extraction of other tables (e.g., users' credentials).

verdict.guard_found: none. list.php:5-6 has no allowlist, quoting, or binding. The safe sibling list_users_safe (list.php:9-12) uses an allowlist, but it is a separate function and does not guard list_users_sorted.
verdict.reason: The trace matches list.php:5-6: `$_GET['sort']` is concatenated into the ORDER BY query with no guard. However, the only occurrences of list_users_sorted in the repo are its definition at list.php:4 (Grep found no call site), so no request in this repo reaches the sink, and whether the injection is exploitable depends on an external caller that I cannot see.
